Ballot Measure Rebuttal Argument Submission Fort8TY OF SAN CARLOS
CITY CLERK'S DEPARTMEN-
If both an argument in favor of and an argument against a measure have been selected for publication in the Sample
Ballot & Official Voter Information Pamphlet, a typed rebuttal to the argument in favor of or the argument against the
measure may be submitted as outlined in this form.
The author(s) of the primary argument of the measure may prepare and submit a rebuttal argument or may authorize
in writing any other person or persons to prepare, submit or sign the rebuttal argument.
A rebuttal argument will not be accepted unless accompanied by this completed form, which shall contain the printed
name(s) and signature(s) of the person(s) submitting it or, if submitted on behalf of a bona fide association of
citizens, the name of the association and the printed name and signature of at least one of its principal officers.
Please make sure you are using proper format before submitting to the City Clerk.
Word count limit for Rebuttal Arguments = 250 words

Rebuttal to Argument in Favor of Measure G
CITY OF SAN CARLOS
CITY CLERK'S DEPARTMEI
[start of argument]
Reject this meritless sales tax hike!
Proponents' argument is authored by a professional municipal PR consultant and cosigned by a
slate of City Hall insiders masquerading as ordinary "residents." But notice: they don't mention
one budget figure. They won't talk numbers, because they can't defend them.
As an independent San Carlos resident, I audited City Hall's figures so you don't have to.
As detailed in our "argument against," City Hall wants to tax us up to 12 times its estimated
budget deficit, totaling $84M!
Behind their usual theater over "public safety" and "emergency services," City Hall wants a
blank-check general tax to fund $200M in capital projects (as stated in their June mailer).
They want to bypass the 213 supermajority requirement for a special tax (or bond) because
they know they lack voter buy-in. Worse, this deficit stems from councilmembers' bad choices:
They paid consultants $200,000 to market this tax to us.
e They are spending $7M for Harrington Park "upgrades" — replacing natural kids' play
spaces with concrete, and only backing down from a $1 M water fountain after public
outcry.
• They want to fund an absurdly overpriced $112M bicycle crossing over Highway 101.
Don't be fooled by their spin on "iocal control" — true local control means keeping $6M/year in
our community to protect local businesses, not funding councilmembers' pet projects.
Otherwise, San Carlos families will be stuck paying for their extravagance on every online order,
delivery, and vehicle purchase — for 14 years!
Force City Hall to change its spending priorities. Vote NO!
[end of argument]
